plants.name: Paeonia officinalis
plants.description: Bowl-shaped blooms 10–13 cm across open in deep crimson to rich pink, with a boss of golden stamens at the center. They sit above glossy, deeply divided leaves and look like silk pompoms. A cottage-garden favorite for centuries.
plants.location: Gardens and meadows across Europe, where the plant is native, and in temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and flower for decades in the same spot. Some garden clumps outlast the people who planted them.

plants.name: Rhododendron macrophyllum
plants.description: Rounded clusters of ruffled, rose-pink blossoms with freckled throats light up the shaded conifer forests of the Pacific coast. Each trusses sits on leathery evergreen foliage. The bloom moves slowly up the mountainsides as spring advances.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to May at lower elevations, later higher up
plants.location: West of the Cascades, from southern British Columbia to northern California, including the Olympic Peninsula and Puget Sound islands
plants.funFact: It is the state flower of Washington, and in May its blooms brighten forest trails that stay green all year.

plants.name: Rosa rugosa
plants.description: This tough seaside shrub has crinkled, deeply veined leaves and wide, five-petaled flowers in rose pink or white. Each flower is crowned with 200 or more yellow stamens and has a strong, sweet perfume. After flowering it carries plump red hips.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May through July, with scattered rebloom until frost
plants.location: Native to the coasts of eastern Russia, Japan, Korea and northern China. It is widely grown and naturalized on temperate shorelines and in gardens.
plants.funFact: The plant thrives in salt spray and sandy soil, so it is often grown to stabilize dunes. Its vitamin-rich hips are used in jams and teas.
